title: Decidability of conjunctive-query entailment in SROIQ
formal: Does one total algorithm decide, for every finite SROIQ knowledge base K and every Boolean conjunctive query q, whether K⊨q under the standard semantics over all finite or infinite models?
definitions: Fix classical SROIQ without datatypes, using the syntax of Horrocks–Kutz–Sattler (2006), Definitions 1–6. Concept names denote subsets of a nonempty domain; nominal concept names denote singletons; individual names denote elements, without a unique-name assumption. Role names denote binary relations, inverse roles reverse their arguments, and U denotes the universal relation. Concepts are built from names, ⊤, ⊥, Boolean operations, ∃r.C and ∀r.C, qualified number restrictions ≥k s.C and ≤k s.C, and ∃s.Self. The last three require a simple role s. They mean, respectively, at least or at most k distinct s-successors satisfying C, and an s-edge from an element to itself. The nonnegative integer k is encoded in binary. K consists of concept inclusions C⊑D, individual assertions C(a), r(a,b), ¬r(a,b), a≠b, and a legal role box. Role inclusions have form w⊑R, with R a non-universal role name and w a nonempty string of non-universal roles, interpreted by relational composition. Regularity requires a strict partial order ≺ on roles satisfying S≺R iff Inv(S)≺R, such that each inclusion has w=RR, w=Inv(R), or w=S₁…Sₜ, RS₁…Sₜ, or S₁…SₜR with every Sᵢ≺R. Equivalent roles can first be identified. Transitivity and symmetry are represented by RR⊑R and Inv(R)⊑R. A role is non-simple if a composition of length at least two is included in it, or in one of its subroles, closing under inverse; all other roles are simple. Reflexivity assertions are allowed; irreflexivity, strict asymmetry and role-disjointness assertions require simple roles. U cannot occur in role-box assertions. These are the standard global regularity and simplicity restrictions, not unrestricted role-chain rules. The query is q=∃x₁…xₜ ∧ⱼαⱼ, where each atom is A(u) or r(u,v), A is a concept name, r is a role name, and terms are variables or individual names. Query roles may be non-simple. Query atoms have no negation, inequality or regular-path operators; variables may receive the same value. A model satisfies q when some assignment makes every atom true. K⊨q means every model of K satisfies q, including infinite models; an inconsistent K entails every query. Both K and q are input, and the sought algorithm must halt on every legal pair, with no prescribed complexity bound.
answer_criterion: Give a terminating, correct yes/no procedure for every legal input (K,q), or prove this decision problem undecidable. A procedure restricted to simple query roles, a Horn fragment, finite models, or cases where an auxiliary construction happens to terminate does not settle the stated problem.
context:
A knowledge base describes incomplete information about a world. Its assertions name some objects, while its general axioms can require additional unnamed objects in every possible world. A Boolean query asks whether a finite relational pattern must exist. The problem is to decide whether the pattern follows from the whole specification, rather than whether it can be found among explicitly stored facts.

For example, let K assert Person(a) and Person⊑∃knows.Person. Every model then contains a person who knows a person, so K entails ∃x∃y(Person(x)∧knows(x,y)∧Person(y)). No named witness for y is needed. The same individual may serve as both variables when the model permits it. More complicated queries reuse variables across several edges, requiring a single assignment that satisfies all joins simultaneously.

SROIQ combines concept negation, existential and universal restrictions, singleton concepts, inverse roles, counting and regular role chains. This expressive combination underlies the logical core of OWL 2 DL. The role restrictions in the definitions are substantive: removing regularity or allowing arbitrary counting over composite roles produces different logics. The original SROIQ paper supplies a decision procedure for consistency, but that alone does not answer arbitrary conjunctive queries.

One might try to test whether K together with ¬q is inconsistent. The difficulty is that the negation of an arbitrary joined relational pattern need not be expressible as a SROIQ knowledge base. Likewise, a finite graph built by a consistency tableau is usually a compact representation of models, not an ordinary database on which evaluating q automatically gives the right answer. Unfolding repeated nodes can change whether a query cycle exists.

Rudolph and Glimm resolved a major part of the surrounding question in 2010. They handle nominals, inverse roles and counting together, and obtain decidability for SROIQ when all binary query predicates are simple roles. Thus the mere presence of those three constructors is not the remaining obstacle. The full question on this card also allows the query to inspect roles affected by transitivity and more general role compositions.

A different positive frontier comes from Horn restrictions. Ortiz, Rudolph and Šimkus show decidability even for a stronger path-query language over Horn-SROIQ, with doubly exponential combined complexity. Horn knowledge bases exclude forms of disjunctive choice that full SROIQ permits. Their result is therefore highly relevant progress, while leaving the unrestricted combination of knowledge-base features and query joins unresolved.

The distinction between all models and finite models is particularly consequential. Rudolph proves undecidability of finite conjunctive-query entailment already in a fragment of SROIQ. This is not an undecidability proof for the semantics chosen here: the sets of countermodels differ, and the distinction can affect the answer even on a small example.

To see the difference directly, require every domain element to have exactly one r-successor and at most one r-predecessor, and require a named element a to have no predecessor. The role r can be simple. Such a knowledge base has an infinite model, the natural-number successor chain, but no finite model: on a finite set, an injective total successor function would be surjective. A fresh predicate A may be empty in the infinite model, so ∃x A(x) is not entailed over all models. Over finite models it is vacuously entailed, because there are none.

Steigmiller and Glimm’s 2019 absorption method addresses practical entailment checking in very expressive logics and is implemented in Konclude. Its termination argument depends on a bounded supply of newly generated nominals in the difficult feature combination. Useful empirical behavior and termination on substantial fragments do not establish a total procedure for every SROIQ input. This conditional termination is exactly why the inherited source continues to present full decidability as open.

There is relevant progress as recently as 2026, but on a different slice of the language. Ibáñez-García, Jung, Michielini and Murlak show that conjunctive-query entailment for S, which adds transitive roles to ALC, is 2ExpTime-complete; hardness already uses two transitive roles and a Boolean conjunctive query. Their May 2026 full version also treats restrictions giving smaller upper bounds. This settles a complexity question for S, not the decidability of full SROIQ.

A positive solution would establish that general finite query patterns can always be answered against this expressive ontology language in principle. A negative solution would identify a sharp gap between consistency checking and pattern entailment inside a standard logical framework. Either outcome would clarify which expressive features can be combined while retaining an algorithmic foundation for querying incomplete knowledge.
why: A basic decidability boundary for querying expressive ontologies: the logic has decidable consistency, but unrestricted conjunctive-query entailment still lacks a general resolution.

importance.reason: A longstanding foundational question connecting description logics, database queries and infinite-model reasoning, with sharply different outcomes for nearby restrictions.

progress.text: Horrocks–Kutz–Sattler define SROIQ and prove decidability of its standard consistency reasoning tasks.
Rudolph–Glimm establish query decidability with nominals, inverses and counting, including SROIQ queries restricted to simple roles.
Ortiz–Rudolph–Šimkus establish decidable path-query answering for Horn-SROIQ.
Rudolph proves finite-model conjunctive-query entailment undecidable in a SROIQ fragment; this uses finite semantics.
Steigmiller–Glimm present absorption-based checking, while explicitly retaining the full decidability question and a termination condition involving new nominals.
The revised full version of the AAAI 2026 paper proves 2ExpTime-completeness for S, including Boolean-query hardness with two transitive roles.

status_note: Reviewed through 11 September 2026. No general decision procedure or undecidability proof for Boolean CQ entailment over all SROIQ models was found in the checked sources. Simple-role queries, Horn fragments, finite-model undecidability and the 2026 complexity result for S concern distinct restricted problems.
